assessment.title: Water Cycle Assessment
assessment.subject: Earth Science
assessment.description: Assessment on the water cycle and its processes

studentResponse: {"rawAnswer":{"explanationQuestion":"The water cycle is a continuous process that moves water through different states and locations on Earth. It involves several key processes: evaporation (liquid to gas), condensation (gas to liquid), precipitation (water falling from clouds), and collection (water gathering in oceans, lakes, etc.). Solar energy drives evaporation, while cooling causes condensation. The cycle is essential for distributing fresh water across the planet and maintaining Earth's climate.","observationQuestion":"I conducted a week-long weather observation project and recorded daily precipitation, temperature, and humidity levels. I noticed that on days with high humidity (above 80%), we often had rain or fog the next day. I also observed that after heavy rain, the air felt fresher and the temperature was slightly cooler. This helped me understand how the water cycle affects local weather patterns."}}
